text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Norway's Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland was given a red-carpet welcome in Hanoi on Wednesday at the start of the first visit to Vietnam by a Norwegian leader.
-- The construction of a new terminal at Hanoi's Noi Bai International airport won't be completed in 1997 as planned because of a lack of capital and construction equipment.
-- Vietnam's Ministry of Planning and Investment has revoked a licence given to a Swiss-Vietnamese joint venture in Ho Chi Minh City for a $216 million commercial centre.
-- Hanoi has set itself a target of 4-4.5 percent annual growth for its agricultural sector and 19-20 percent annual growth for industry between 1996-2000.
-- Japan's International Cooperation Agency and the Ministry of Science, Technology and Environment have held a symposium on plans for high technology zones in Vietnam.
-- Vietnam's Youth Union marked its 40th anniversary on Wednesday with a meeting in Hanoi to review a two-year campaign aimed at encouraging young people to take part in social activities.
-- Flood waters in southern Vietnam's Mekong Delta have risen rapidly and are approaching their highest levels in 20 years.
-- Hanoi's streets have been cleaned, decorative lights installed, more fresh water supplied and pavements repaired to mark the 42nd anniversary on Thursday of the city's liberation.
